top_strength: Nicole opened by handing the customer the agenda and then asking what mattered most to her — "what are your biggest concerns and what are the most important things you want answers to on this call today?" — which surfaced the elevator reservation, the discarded bed frame and the TV box question early instead of at the end. She was also unusually clean on the trip fee, framing it as the single exception rather than burying it: "there's only one thing outside of the hourly rate which is a one time travel fee of $70." The long-walk probing was thorough — she pushed for park-to-elevator and elevator-to-door distances at both ends before committing to a number.
coaching_note: The whole Save Your Ass prep speech is missing, and this was the ideal call for it — the customer said "this is my first time doing this as well" and told Nicole she was packing her own small items. A first-time self-packer on a 6th-floor-to-10th-floor move with long walks at both ends is exactly who benefits from "prep before move day means a shorter move and a lower bill," plus the consolidation examples and the take-a-carload tip. Nicole quoted 4-5 hours and $838-$1,030 with no lever offered to bring that down. Add the prep speech right after the estimate, before the booking ask.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently polite and responsive with frequent "Awesome" affirmations, but transactional — she never used the customer's name and let the "this is my first time doing this" cue pass without any reassurance.
